lean.fidelity_note: Let $K(s)=320b(s+1)$ with integer $b\ge1$, $q_1=1$, $\lambda_0=N\ge\mathcal B(1)$, and use the frequency recurrence and maximum rule of (1.14). The formal statement assumes only that $\mathcal B(s)>0$ and $\log\mathcal B(s)\ge4K(s+1)^3$ at positive indices. It proves $q_j\le q_{j+1}\le q_j+1$, $q_j\to\infty$, and $4\log\lambda_{j+2}\le(\log\lambda_{j-1})^2$ for every $j\ge1$. The last formula is exactly $L_{j+1}\le(\log\lambda_{j-1})^2$, because $L_i=4\log\lambda_{i+1}$. In §1.5 the paper also takes $\mathcal B$ nondecreasing and large enough to dominate all fixed-order analytic constants, and fixes $b$ from the later construction. Those extra restrictions are not needed for this arithmetic theorem. The conclusion therefore applies under fewer hypotheses, with the same index range and bound. The maximum is an actual greatest admissible integer, not an arbitrary eligible choice.
lean.name: TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_1_3
